title: Armstrong as fourth trumpet with no parts at the Lafayette
summary: Waters remembers Armstrong sitting in the Henderson trumpet section with no part to read until his solo break, which brought the house down.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: middle, yeah, somethin' like that. Well, I remember Louie at this Lafayette Theater, and I remember him real well because he didn't have no parts, that's what I remembered so well. He didn't have no parts to read because it's, he was the fourth trumpet added on, because they had the Luke brothers in the band, three Luke brothers -
Three Smith brothers, Luke Smith, Russell Smith -

Yeah, I get all mixed up, yeah. Smith brothers, all three of them playin' trumpet - one playin' first trumpet and the oth-, and Luke and Joe, that's what the trumpet section, that I remember real well, you know. And Louie was up there, sittin' up there, just sitting down and didn't, wasn't doing nothing, 'cause he didn't have no parts. I don't know if Louie could read then - I know, that I don't know nothin' about, see. It's just the parts for that he couldn't read, but even if he could have read he, they didn't have no parts for, because they didn't write no fourth parts for trumpet at that period, you now. Fletcher didn't, no fourth parts.
Or even third part, well, 'cause when Louie -

You were kinda complicated with third parts even. But fourth parts was out of the question at that period. Now, I mean, they write all kind of things. But - so Louie was like this - I remember this real well. Then it would come to a break, see, for Louie to go into his solo. And he'd stand up and make a break, (scats), and the people just roared, I never hear so much noise in my life, you know, see. That I remember real well.
